8 recommended Lumecca clinics in Shinjuku! Compare prices and options

 

"I want to receive Lumecca in Shinjuku, but I don't know which clinic to choose."

"I want to know not only the initial fee, but also the costs and irradiation details for the second and subsequent treatments."

There are medical institutions around Shinjuku where you can receive IPL (light therapy), but not all of them have introduced Lumecca.

Lumecca is InMode's IPL device, and is a treatment that adjusts irradiation conditions according to skin concerns such as age spots, freckles, and redness.

In this article, we will compare 8 clinics around Shinjuku whose information about Lumecca can be found on the official website, in terms of treatment fees, location, and precautions.

We will also explain the number of treatments, downtime, and things to check when signing a contract.

Let's compare not only the price, but also whether the clinic handles Lumecca, including the irradiation range, number of treatments, and consultation fees.

What you can learn from this article
  • Lumecca features and precautions
  • 4 things to check when choosing a clinic
  • 8 clinics that guide you through Lumecca around Shinjuku
  • Price comparison and estimation of multiple hospital visits
Supervisor of this article

Yoshitomo Chihara

Director of Norris Beauty Clinic

Postdoctoral Researcher, Norris Cancer Center, University of Southern California;National Cancer Center PathologyHead of the club,Nara Prefectural Medical UniversityLecturer in Molecular Pathology,Saiseikai Chuwa HospitalAfter serving as head of the urology departmentnorris beauty clinicOpened a hospital.

Norris Beauty Clinic’s content production policy regarding aesthetic medicine

Norris Beauty Clinic operates with the aim of disseminating accurate and easy-to-understand information to our readers about aesthetic medicine, such as medical diets (GLP-1 receptor agonists, fat freezing, fat-dissolving injections, liposuction, etc.) and double plastic surgery.

Cosmetic treatments such as medical diets and double plastic surgery are important themes that are closely related to each individual's health condition, constitution, cost, and schedule.

We create content with an emphasis on reliability, neutrality, and safety so that our readers can calmly make choices that are suitable for them and prepare for advance counseling.

■Basic policy for content production

■Production flow

At our media, we create content through the following process.

Production flow
  1. Search needs/concerns survey
  2. Configuration design (organizing comparison standards and points to note)
  3. Writing/editing/fact checking
  4. Regular updates of fees and medical treatment system

■Regarding reliability of information

When writing articles, we use the following public institutions and highly reliable information sources.

An example of reference data for this media
  • Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare(Medical advertising guidelines/Pharmaceuticals Act related information)
  • PMDA (Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency)
  • Japan Obesity Society・Japanese Society of Aesthetic Surgery (JSAS)Related academic societies such as
  • Consumer Affairs Agency(Related to the Specified Commercial Transactions Act and the Act on Premiums and Representations)
  • Official website information of each medical institution/pharmaceutical company

In addition, we regularly review information in response to price revisions, changes in clinic hours, updated guidelines, etc.

■Commitment to neutrality and transparency

Guaranteeing neutrality and objectivity
  • Specifies not only the benefits of each treatment but also side effects, risks, and downtime.
  • Presents points to note regarding total costs and cancellation regulations (cooling-off, etc.) for free medical treatment.
  • Do not use definitive expressions such as ``always'' or ``absolutely'' regarding changes or progress that vary from person to person.
  • Information is posted based on objective facts regardless of whether there is a partnership or not.

For detailed management structure and editorial stance, please seeNorris Beauty Clinic’s content production policy regarding aesthetic medicinePlease check.

Management information of Norris Beauty Clinic

Lumecca is an IPL (light therapy) device.

Lumecca is InMode's IPL device that irradiates light with a wide range of wavelengths to target melanin pigments and the redness of blood vessels.

The characteristics of the light are different from lasers, and a doctor will determine whether it is suitable for multiple concerns such as age spots and redness.

Because products differ in the specifications of the filters and devices used, it is not possible to conclude that one device is superior to another based on the wavelength values alone.

Things to know about Lumecca
  • Adaptation to age spots, freckles, and redness
  • The number of treatments varies depending on the skin condition
  • Pigment reaction and skin care after treatment

Even with the treatment called "light therapy," the device name, settings, and irradiation range vary depending on the medical institution.

When making a reservation for Lumecca, please check the name of the equipment actually used, not the general IPL treatment information.

If you clarify in advance whether the area you are concerned about is brown stains, redness, or both, it will be easier to communicate your goals during the consultation.

Even for similar color changes, different treatments may be chosen depending on the type of lesion diagnosed by your doctor.

In addition to the necessity of the treatment, be sure to receive an explanation of the expected reactions after irradiation, the conditions that will require the next visit, and the cost burden.

It is important to choose a treatment based on the condition of your skin, rather than making a decision based solely on the popularity of the device.

Addresses multiple skin concerns such as age spots, freckles, and redness

Since IPL utilizes the reaction to melanin and hemoglobin, problems related to pigment and blood vessels can be discussed in the same treatment.

However, the effects and appropriate treatment vary depending on the type, depth, and skin color of the stain.

If you suspect that you have melasma, please consult your doctor before the procedure, as irradiation may worsen pigmentation.

Not all things that look like stains are the same lesion, so it is important to conduct an examination before deciding on a treatment device.

Even when it comes to problems related to pigments, it is not possible to predict the reaction to irradiation just by the density visible on the surface.

For skin affected by sunburn or skin with multiple types of pigment spots, the application and irradiation range must be carefully checked.

Regarding redness, treatment strategies may differ depending on temporary redness due to skin type and symptoms related to blood vessels.

Please be specific about the area and symptoms, such as ``I want to consult about a stain on my cheek'' or ``I'm concerned about the redness around my nose.''

During your consultation, ask if there are any areas that cannot be irradiated or if other methods are suitable.

It is important to decide what to prioritize and not think that Lumecca alone can solve all skin problems at the same time.

The difference from conventional IPL equipment lies in the irradiation characteristics and settings.

Lumecca is an IPL device with features such as irradiation energy and wavelength filter.

The explanation in the advertisement, such as "you can feel the effect after a small number of treatments," will vary depending on your skin type, type of lesion, and treatment conditions.

It is not possible to make a uniform comparison such as 5 to 10 times with conventional equipment and 3 to 5 times with Lumecca.

Plan your hospital visit after receiving an explanation of the expected number of irradiations and side effects.

Higher output does not necessarily mean higher safety or effectiveness, and there are risks such as burns, blisters, and pigmentation.

The device's output and filter characteristics are factors that doctors consider when considering settings to suit your skin condition.

Even if the same Lumecca is used, if the irradiation area, number of irradiations, and output settings are different, the post-treatment reaction and hospital visit plan may change.

The advertised frequency guidelines do not guarantee the same results for all symptoms.

At your first consultation, we will ask you what kind of changes you can expect after one treatment, and what to consider next if the improvement is not sufficient.

If you have multiple visits, it is important to evaluate your skin's reaction each time and revise your treatment plan if necessary.

Rather than comparing the idea that fewer sessions are better, consider risks and costs when deciding.

Although it addresses uneven skin tone across the entire face, there are differences in reactions after the treatment.

With plans that support whole-face irradiation, areas with spots and redness can be treated all at once.

After irradiation, the stain may temporarily appear darker or a small scab-like change may appear.

These reactions do not occur in everyone, and the success or failure of treatment cannot be determined solely by the magnitude of the change.

Please do not rub the irradiated area vigorously and continue to moisturize and take precautions against UV rays as instructed by the treatment clinic.

Even with a full-face plan, there may be areas to avoid irradiation, such as areas near the eyelids or mucous membranes.

Therefore, just because the price list says "all face" does not mean that we can treat all areas of your concern.

Before making your appointment, be sure to check the target area, and let us know if you have any particular areas of concern, such as your cheeks or nose, during your consultation.

Even if the color appears darker after irradiation, do not forcefully rub or peel the skin, and observe the progress as instructed by your clinic.

If you experience symptoms that are different from those normally described, such as blisters or strong pain, do not continue to monitor the situation on your own and contact the clinic.

When comparing photos before treatment, it is important to evaluate them taking into account differences in lighting and shooting conditions.

4 points to check before choosing a Lumecca clinic in Shinjuku

Even at clinics that offer Lumecca, the conditions vary, such as whether to irradiate the entire face or a portion of the face, how many rounds to irradiate, and who the practitioner is.

When comparing prices, be sure to check not only the initial price and regular price, but also the consultation fee and additional treatment costs.

4 items to compare
  • Irradiation range and number of laps
  • Initial and regular charges
  • Practitioner and medical system
  • Travel distance from the station

When making comparisons, first let's sort out the reason why you want Lumecca and the area where you expect to visit the hospital.

The plans needed are not necessarily the same for those who have a limited range of age spots and those who want to consult about uneven color across their face.

Even if the initial fee seems low, your budget may change if you include consultation fees, optional fees, and subsequent fees.

Items that cannot be confirmed on the official website should not be treated as conditions that can be directly compared, and it is important to inquire at the time of reservation.

Transportation costs if you need to go to the hospital and the days of the week when you can make a reservation will also affect how easy it is to continue.

If you get estimates based on the same conditions and compare the treatment details, costs, and ease of access, it will be easier to narrow down the options that suit you.

Check the irradiation range, number of laps, and number of shots

The range of charges varies even for the same Lumecca, such as full face, cheek only, and additional spots.

The number of irradiation shots varies depending on the specifications of the device, the area of the face, the condition of the skin, and the irradiation method, so there is no standard number that is common throughout the country.

Rather than simply assuming that a large number of shots will be effective, ask for explanations about the target area, number of irradiation cycles, and irradiation settings.

Confirmation items for treatment details
  • Full face or partial irradiation?
  • How many rounds of irradiation are included in one price?
  • Practitioner qualifications and doctor examination system
  • Is there a cost for additional irradiation or re-examination?

"One round" is used to describe one round of the same area, but it is not a unified fee classification down to the detailed irradiation method for each area.

When you receive a suggestion to increase the number of treatments, ask specifically what skin concern it is intended to address.

Even if you compare the price for just the cheeks and the price for the whole face, it is not possible to simply tell which one is better or worse because the scope of treatment is different.

Even if the official website says ``full face,'' you can reduce confusion by checking how much of the forehead, nose, face line, etc. is included.

There are plans where the cost changes as the number of trips or laps increases, so be sure to check the conditions under which additional fees will be incurred during your consultation.

What is important is not the number of shots, but the irradiation plan and risk explanation based on the examination.

Compare the total amount of the first charge and the regular charge from the second time onwards.

If you sign up for multiple courses based only on the initial price, your budget may differ from what you had planned.

If the first time is 9,800 yen and the second and subsequent times are 18,000 yen, the total for the five times is 81,800 yen.

If the first time is 15,000 yen and the second and subsequent times are 15,000 yen each, the total for the five times will be 75,000 yen.

If there are conditions such as coupon tickets, limited time prices, or consultation fees, please compare the total amount including each.

The table above is an assumption for explaining fee calculations and is not a fee schedule for a specific clinic.

For example, if a clinic applies a special fee only for the first time, the single fee may change from the second application.

Therefore, if you are considering multiple visits from the beginning, please separate the payment amount for one visit and the estimated amount for the entire hospital visit.

If a course fee is set, you need to check not only the amount compared to a single payment, but also the expiration date and how reservations will be changed.

Compare whether the treatment fee includes consultation fees, options such as anesthesia, and re-examination costs in case of skin problems.

If you receive a proposal that exceeds your budget, we can discuss the scope and number of treatments after confirming the necessity.

Please separate whether the price is low and whether the treatment is suitable for your concerns.

Check the qualifications of the person in charge of the doctor's examination and irradiation

For medical IPL irradiation, a doctor determines the suitability, and a doctor or a nurse under the doctor's direction may perform the treatment.

There is no evidence to link the fact that nurses are in charge of safety.

Check the qualifications of the practitioner, the contact system in case of skin problems, and whether you can consult with a doctor before the treatment.

Although the quality of the treatment cannot be determined solely by the type of person in charge, it is possible to confirm who will examine the patient and who will perform the irradiation.

Check to see if your skin condition and medical history can be fully confirmed during the examination, and if the irradiation conditions are explained.

It will be easier to think about what to do if you find out who will be in charge of the consultation, how to contact you, and the cost of re-examination when skin redness or pigmentation occurs.

Even if you are seeing your doctor for the first time, ask if you can discuss any changes in your skin condition at subsequent visits.

An important deciding factor is whether there is a system in place to ask the doctor for confirmation if the practitioner cannot answer your questions.

Don't just compare qualifications alone; check the process from consultation to treatment.

In addition to Shinjuku Station, consider Yotsuya and Shinjuku Gyoemmae areas as candidates.

Travel time around Shinjuku Station varies depending on the exit.

The eight clinics introduced this time include not only clinics near Shinjuku Station, but also clinics around Shinjuku Gyoemmae Station and Yotsuya Sanchome Station.

Before making a reservation, check the address and nearest station to make sure you can easily commute from your home or workplace.

Even for clinics in Shinjuku Ward, the location that is easiest to access will change depending on whether you are walking from JR Shinjuku Station or using the Marunouchi Line or Toei Shinjuku Line.

There are many exits around Shinjuku Station, so checking the nearest exit listed on the official website will make it easier to get directions.

For clinics near Yotsuya 3-chome or Shinjuku Gyoen-mae, it may be more convenient to go directly from your home or workplace rather than transferring from Shinjuku Station.

If you plan to walk outdoors in strong sunlight for a long time after your treatment, consider taking measures to protect yourself from UV rays while traveling.

If you are likely to visit more than once, it is important to be able to make reservations on the days of your choice, such as weekday nights or holidays.

Please compare prices and location and choose a clinic that you can easily attend.

8 clinics where you can receive Lumecca near Shinjuku

The following are clinics where you can check the information about Rumecca on their official website.

Prices vary depending on the scope of treatment, number of laps, special rate application conditions, and initial consultation fee, so the posted amount may not necessarily match the actual total amount paid.

When making a reservation, please check to see if the clinic you are requesting still offers the same menu.

The prices in the comparison table are not rankings based on the same number of treatments and the same irradiation area.

For example, the contents included in the fee will differ between clinics that offer one round of full-face treatment and clinics that offer two rounds of irradiation.

You will also need to check with each hospital the cost of returning home after just a consultation, initial conditions, and expiration dates for multiple-visit plans.

Also, even if treatments are introduced on the official website, the dates and times available for reservations and the staff in charge may change.

Once you find a clinic you are interested in, check the implementation status of Lumecca and the total payment amount before making a reservation.

In the individual introductions below, we have separated the officially announced features and points you should check before visiting the hospital.

Lula Beauty Clinic Shinjuku Clinic | Information on handling Lumecca on the official website

On the official website of Lula Beauty Clinic, the initial price and regular price for Lumecca's full face are shown.

The price for the 5-session course is also shown, but there may be payment methods and application conditions attached to using the course.

Check the range of irradiation, the number of laps, and the conditions covered by the set fee before comparing.

Confirmation information before visiting the hospital
  • Address: 8th floor, Equinia Shinjuku Building, 1-1-17 Kabukicho, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
  • Price information: Full face: first time 10,780 yen, regular 16,500 yen (tax included)
  • Note: The whole face must be covered once. Limited time price is subject to separate conditions.

Lula Beauty Clinic provides information on the Shinjuku clinic, and Lumecca's price list lists single-time and multiple-time courses for the entire face.

When comparing 5-course courses, check not only the total cost of the first and regular one-time fees, but also the terms and conditions of the course.

The official price list also includes notes on how to pay for the course and how to complete the course on the day.

If you see some conditional prices, check the difference from the regular price and the applicable conditions to avoid misunderstandings when making comparisons.

Also, be sure to ask at the time of your consultation whether the dark spots you are concerned about are eligible for full-face irradiation, and the cost if additional irradiation is required.

After receiving an explanation of the redness and pigment reaction after the treatment, consider the method of visiting the hospital that fits your schedule.

Click here for the official website of Lula Beauty Clinic Shinjuku-in

HAKU Beauty Clinic Shinjukuin | Information on handling Lumecca on the official website

HAKU Beauty Clinic near Shinjuku Station posts the initial price and regular price for a full facial on its official page.

The 5-course course costs 45,000 yen (tax included) and must be used within 6 months from the date of first use.

The initial consultation fee is 2,000 yen, but the official website states that there is no charge if you receive the treatment on the same day.

Confirmation information before visiting the hospital
  • Location: 1-10-2 Nishi-Shinjuku, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo, 110 Building, B1F
  • Price information: Full face: first time 9,800 yen, regular 12,000 yen (tax included)
